title: Device posture across products: Client Connector evaluates, Private Access and Internet & SaaS consume

prose.text: A posture question usually crosses three products: Client Connector runs the checks, and Private Access rules and Internet & SaaS trust levels act on the result. This subject walks that split and points at where each part is held.

steps.label: Where is the profile defined, and who uses it?
steps.text: One definition serves both products: [[zpa.posture-profiles.object-model:zcc-defined]] It is evaluated on the device: [[zcc.device-posture:evaluated-on-device]]

steps.label: Which checks exist on which platform?
steps.text: Pass conditions and version floors are in [[zcc.device-posture.check-types]], and the per-platform lists in [[zcc.device-posture.platform-support]]. A type the selected platform does not support cannot be added to the profile: [[zcc.device-posture.check-types:platform-selection]] Ownership Variable and Unauthorized Modification are Android and iOS checks, not Windows ones: [[zcc.device-posture.check-types:ownership-variable]], [[zcc.device-posture.check-types:unauthorized-modification]], [[zcc.device-posture.platform-support:windows-types]].

steps.label: When is it evaluated?
steps.text: Schedule, frequency setting and trigger events: [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:cadence]], [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:frequency-setting]], [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:triggers]]. {{immediate-only-five}} What a shorter frequency costs on the device is open {{gap:frequency-cost}}.

steps.label: What happens to a session already open?
steps.text: Existing connections are not affected by a posture update: [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:cadence]] Whether a Private Access reauthentication timeout bounds how stale the result can be is open: [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:reauth-bounds-staleness]].

steps.label: Does it apply before login, or to a partner tenant?
steps.text: The pre-login machine tunnel evaluates only the types listed for it: [[zpa.machine-tunnels.posture:windows-types]], [[zpa.machine-tunnels.posture:macos-types]]. What the machine tunnel does with a profile's other types is open {{gap:machine-tunnel-unlisted-types}}, and so is why they are excluded: [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:user-context-types]]. Partner tenant tunnels are covered only when the profile says so: [[zcc.device-posture.check-types:partner-tenant]]

prose.text: An access rule names the profile by its posture UDID and asks for VERIFIED or VERIFICATION FAILED: [[zpa.posture-profiles.policy-operand]]. Posture condition sets in one rule are joined by AND, and profiles inside one set by OR unless toggled: [[zpa.policy.conditions:and-within-some-criteria]] Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins: [[zpa.policy.access-rule-order:segment-group-allow-shadows-deny]] {{posture-and-trusted-network}} Timeout rules can tier sessions by posture too: [[zpa.policy.timeout-rules:posture-tiering-example]]
Internet & SaaS policy uses posture through device trust levels, which are rule criteria in several policies: [[shared.device-posture.trust-levels]].

A check that failed, could not run, or has not been refreshed are separated in [[zcc.device-posture.failure-modes]]. Whether a missing CrowdStrike ZTA score fails the check is open: [[zcc.device-posture.failure-modes:zta-score-absent]].

checks.do: For a device that passed yesterday and fails today: whether the type re-evaluates immediately or waits for the frequency or a trigger event (new network, Wi-Fi change, reboot), and when it last ran.
Whether the posture change moved the user to a different access rule in order, rather than failing one rule; put the strictest posture rule above the laxer ones.
For a session that survived a posture failure: whether the connection predates the failure, since existing connections keep the earlier result.
For a pre-login machine tunnel failing posture: whether Apply to Windows or macOS Machine Tunnel is selected, and whether every type in the profile is on that platform's machine tunnel list.
For a rule that combines posture with a trusted network: whether both conditions hold for the user, and whether an on-premises rule without posture sits above it.

immediate-only-five.statement: Only Process Check, Detect Carbon Black, Detect CrowdStrike, Detect SentinelOne and Detect Microsoft Defender are re-evaluated as soon as the posture changes on the device; any other type, Full Disk Encryption for example, keeps its last result until the configured frequency or a trigger event runs the evaluation again.
immediate-only-five.conditions: Reads the help's list of immediately evaluated checks as complete; the help gives it as 'the following posture checks' and names no others.

posture-and-trusted-network.statement: A Private Access rule that carries both a posture condition and a trusted network condition matches only when both hold. A rule meant to admit on-premises devices without posture must not carry the posture condition and must be ordered above the rule that checks posture.
posture-and-trusted-network.conditions: Combines the AND between a rule's criteria with first-match rule order; not tested on a tenant.

frequency-cost.title: What a shorter posture evaluation frequency costs on the device
frequency-cost.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The frequency slider goes down to 2 minutes but costs battery + API calls. Zscaler's 15-minute default is the right trade-off for most tenants ... expect client-side resource cost." The help gives the 2 to 15 minute range (zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:frequency-setting) and nothing about cost.
frequency-cost.blocks: advising on a frequency below 15 minutes

machine-tunnel-unlisted-types.title: What the machine tunnel does with a profile's types that are not on its list
machine-tunnel-unlisted-types.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Designing a posture profile that relies on these [Process Check, Detect Defender, Ownership Variable] for pre-login enforcement silently evaluates as 'pass'." The help lists the types that apply to each machine tunnel (zpa.machine-tunnels.posture) and says an unselected type is evaluated only for the Private Access and Internet & SaaS tunnels; it does not say what a pre-login rule sees for a profile that holds an unlisted type. Test with a machine tunnel rule on a profile that holds Process Check.
machine-tunnel-unlisted-types.blocks: telling whether a pre-login posture rule enforces all of a profile's types
